questions.q: Why did Mahatma Gandhi launch the Non-Cooperation Movement in August 1920? Explain.
questions.answer: The massacre aroused the fury of the Indian people. Gandhiji by this time, was convinced that no useful purpose would be served by supporting the government. Gandhiji, therefore, started his non-cooperation movement in August 1920, in which he appealed to the people not to cooperate with the British government.

or.q: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted by Indians? Give two reasons.
or.answer: (1) The Indians boycotted this all-White commission. (2) The Indians considered this Act as an insult to them. Black flags were shown, demonstrations and Hartals took place all over the country and the cry of ‘Simon go back’ was heard.

questions.q: What do you understand by 'Purna Swaraj'?
questions.answer: (1) Purna-Swaraj means complete independence and sovereignty. (2) At the historic annual session of Congress in Lahore in 1929, the Congress committed itself to a demand for Purna-Swaraj or complete independence and issued a call to the country to celebrate 26 th January as Purna-Swaraj Day. On January 26, 1930, the Congress celebrated ‘Independence Day’.

questions.q: Differentiate between the Moderates and the Radicals.
questions.answer: (1) Its leaders had complete faith in the British Government and in its sense of justice. From 1885 to 1905, the Indian National Congress had a very narrow social base. petitions and worked within the framework of law. They did not fulfill the demands of the Moderates. (2) It was Bal Gangadhar Tilak who realized the importance of boycott as a weapon that could be used to paralyze the whole British administrative machinery in India. Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal (Lal-Bal-Pal) were important leaders of this Radical group. Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave a slogan ‘Freedom is our birth right and we must have it’. Moderates believed in petition and requesting the British government to solve the grievances whereas Radicals believed in organizing mass protests, criticizing government policies, boycotting foreign goods and use of Swadeshi goods.

questions.q: Why did Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt throw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
questions.answer: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb inside the Central Legislative Assembly on 8th April, 1929 protesting against the passage of the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill while raising slogans of Inquilab Zindabad (long live the revolution), though no one was killed or injured in the bomb incident.

This led to the formation of Indian National Congress in the year 1885.

Response: (2) All these factors helped in the spread of Nationalism among the people of India. Widespread agitation ensued in the streets and in the press. This opposition was carried on by organized meetings, processions and demonstrations etc. (3) Hindus and Muslims tied ‘rakhi’ on each other’s hands to show their unity and their protest. Other protests were violent and aggressive in nature. (4) the Swadeshi and Boycott movements — foreign goods were boycotted and swadeshi mills, banks and stores set up, with students and women taking part. Spirit: it showed that nationalism had become a mass feeling, that people were united across religions, self-reliant and no longer afraid of repression; the British had to annul the partition in 1911.

questions.q: Describe the role of Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army in the freedom struggle.
questions.answer: (1) He found the outbreak of the Second World War to be a convenient opportunity to strike a blow for the freedom of India. (2) Bose had been put under house arrest in 1940 but he managed to escape to Berlin on March 28, 1941. The Indian community there acclaimed him as the leader (Netaji). He was greeted with ‘Jai Hind’ (Salute to the motherland). (3) On an invitation from Ras Bihari Bose, Subhash Chandra Bose came to East Asia on June 13, 1943. He was made president of the Indian Independence League and the leader of the INA popularly called ‘Azad Hind Fauj’. (4) He promised independence to Indians saying, ‘tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe Azadi dunga’ (You give me blood, I will give you freedom). (5) In March 1944, the Indian flag was hoisted at Kohima. (6) Though the INA collapsed, its patriotism inspired Indians and shook British confidence in the loyalty of Indian soldiers.
